messages:
maria gomez: :rotating_light: seeing a crashloop on pool-gpu-east-3, runtime containers keep segfaulting after the 02:00 deploy. vLLM worker processes exit with SIGSEGV.

oncall-bot: Paging oncall-sre -> raj patel (pager level: P1)

raj patel: Ack, I'm on it. Which hosts and any obvious OOMs?

maria gomez: Host list: gpuhost-23, gpuhost-24, gpuhost-26. Logs show `SIGSEGV` in fused attention kernel, plus repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` traces. Not seeing system OOMs in dmesg yet.

sean li: copying logs into thread:```
# tail -n 50 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log
[2026-03-15T02:14:07Z] vllm_worker[4791]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f8a6b2f1c3f sp 00007ffd3a9b5c00 error 4 in libfusedkernels.so[7f8a6b200000+1a000]
[2026-03-15T02:14:08Z] nvml: GPU 0: ECC error count increased
[2026-03-15T02:14:09Z] vllm_worker[4791]: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: kernel launch failed
```

maria gomez: repro on canary model was fine pre-deploy. Deploy was a runtime bump to 1.9.2 with our custom fused kernels.

raj patel: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon gpuhost-23/24/26 to stop new pods 2) scale down runtime replica count in that nodepool 3) roll back runtime to 1.9.1 on affected pools. I'll start cordon now.

ops-sre: I'm running `kubectl cordon gpuhost-23 && kubectl drain gpuhost-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to get pods off, will report back.

maria gomez: customer metrics: a handful of Dedicated customers hitting 504s, approx 4% error spike across region-east. Posting a short note to status once we have rollback confirmation.

raj patel: roll back started: applying runtime image tag `redwood/runtime:1.9.1-rc2` to nodepool-east. Canary scaled to 2, observed one successful generation, no segfaults in last 30s.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-09 - Runtime fused kernel segfault -> container crashloop. Severity: P1. Linked to runbook `runtime-segfaults` and paging history.

sean li: while rollback is in progress I'm going to remove the custom fused kernels from the image and build a debug image with ASAN-like checks and extra GPU bounds logging. Will trigger on a non-prod pool first.

maria gomez: Thanks. Ops: any indications of hardware faults? NVML reported ECC increments earlier. Could be memory corruption on GPU or driver + kernel mismatch.

ops-sre: Running `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0` on gpuhost-23 shows no persistent ECC unrecoverable errors but driver logs show `GPU reset` events at 02:14.

raj patel: For customer comms: initial message drafted — short status page note, "We are investigating increased error rates in East; mitigation underway (rollback). Some customers on dedicated pools may see transient 5xxs." Maria can you post after rollback confirmed?

maria gomez: Will post once rollback completes and we see stable metrics for 5 minutes. Also tagging legal for possible customer impact review. @sean li please attach debug image artifacts when ready.

sean li: uploaded debug tarball to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1769876543/debug-vllm-1.9.2-logs.tar.gz

ops-sre: gpuhost-23 drained. gpuhost-24 and 26 cordoned, pods evicted. No further crashloops on new nodes.

raj patel: Rollback finished at 02:35Z. Observed 0 segfaults in last 3m across the pool.

maria gomez: Status update posted: "Mitigation: rolled back runtime image to 1.9.1, cordoned affected hosts. Impact: transient 5xx errors for a subset of customers in region-east. Ongoing: deeper postmortem and kernel debug. INC number: INC-20260315-09." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager handoff scheduled: oncall-sre -> next-oncall at 03:00Z.

raj patel: Moving to mitigation -> postmortem. Assigning to eng-runtime for kernel debug and to ops-sre for hardware verification.

maria gomez: Thanks all. Closing live incident channel; will reopen if crashloops recur.

ops-sre: Follow-ups: run GPU burn-in on gpuhost-23, collect full driver + dmesg, and validate kernel-module versions.

sean li: I'll open a PR to add conservative fallback to non-fused kernels on runtime startup if GPU assertions appear.

maria gomez: +1, tagging @eng-runtime and @security for the postmortem.

ops-sre: final note: no customer data exposure, no creds involved.```
